note: v2 THE TEAR: kit E2 stretched x2 vs hats in 32nds, tape stop, a one-bar void (cello blur only), then the crest's locked groove and four lights return for seven bars
v7 THE SURGE IS A MENSURATION CANON: E1 at x0.5 (far), x1 (the hook, right through) and x2 (near), from bar 97, realigning every 10 beats; tide 5+3
v8 THE VOICE SINGS BEFORE THE LIFT: the low voice sings its line on E1 (voice-legato, joined, breathing) twice in bars 57-64, kit thins to kick and rim, the crest lifts out of the second go
v9 THE TIDE COMES IN: the head starts on D alone (8+0) and the C creeps in to 4+4 by bar 16; the harmonium lensed in through a low-pass opening from 600 Hz
v12 THE FAR SIDE LETS IT GO: the cello holds one D for 8 bars then lets go; the old voice sings the far side lets it go, go landing on the B-flat bar
v13 THE ANSWER: the old voice answers t5's young voice in the overlap, the tide comes in, A G E D, bars 7 and 11
v16 THE LAST CHORUS: after the stopped tape the choir sings the line in D with a keyed third, twice, voices alone, the old voice joining the second time
v17 THE CANON CONVERGES: far slows into step with the whistle from bar 105, near joins from 109, last four bars E1 in unison across three octaves
v19 THE SQUEEZE SQUEEZES: E2's cell on kit and sequencer loses its rests, seven sixteenths to six (bars 49-52) to five (53-56), wound like a spring before the sung clearing
v23 THE PULL GATHERS THE BAND: E2's cell assembled one hit at a time from the pull's first bar - kick alone, then rim, then snare, then the whole cell; the sequencer joins root first
v24 THE TIDE COMES IN WAVES: the harmonium swells about 4 dB with each swing of the tide, cresting where the chord turns (the split moving 6 5 4 3 2 3 4 5 beats)

v27 SOMETHING MOVES EVERY EIGHT BARS (Harry 23:55): the pull's second half turns to G/Am7, harmonium octave shifts, hats thin then fill, marimba and sequencer drop out and return, open-hat lift and a fill into bar 45
v29 THE TIDE COMES IN IN TWO WAVES: hats only eighths for bars 1-8, then sixteenths; the kora's E5 counter-line grows in from bar 9
v32 THE CHOIR SINGS THE MEETING: 'near and far as one ... all of it at once' on E1 with the three-octave unison
v33 THE TEAR, SUNG: the duet torn apart - the near voice faster each time, the old voice slower, until the void
v35 THE FLOOR TEARS AWAY: bass, fretless and sequencer out under the torn duet's last four bars, back with the last chorus
v37 THE TIDE SINGS HIGH: a falsetto 'ooh' descant (register=1) over the tide's second half, E5 down to G4
v38 THE OLD MAN'S LAST WORD (age 0.8) AND THE TROMBONE SLIDES D-C-Bb under his 'go'
v41 THE SEA DRAWS BACK: harmonium, lights, marimba and kora out for the pull's first eight bars, the floor bare; the wave comes in at bar 25
v45 THE TEAR CLEARS THE ROOM: steel pan, marimba, sequencer and whistle ripped out on the tear's downbeat; harmonium, the torn duet, trombone, stretched kit and floor remain
v47 THE TIDE ON HANDS: the E2 cell on a cajon through the tide (slaps, centre hits, ghosts, palmas); the kit's fill at bar 44 grabs the sticks back
v49 THE LAST CHORUS STARTS ALONE: after the stopped tape the choir sings the first line over only the lights and the sub; the band crashes back in on the second
v50 TIME DILATES AT THE EDGE: the drummer's E2 cell drops to half speed four bars into the out-seam, hats to eighths then quarters, the 303 stops; the last word and the ebb untouched
v52 THE CREST COMES DOWN TO FOUR: the second chorus over a plain four on the floor, snare on two and four, open hats on the off-beats
v53 THE NEAR SIDE SPINS UP: the marimba's E1 trill every fourth note for four bars, every second for four, full from bar 9
v54 THE NEAR SIDE WAKES: the young near voice answers the in-seam's old voice, the tide comes in, an octave up, twice in the gaps after the whistle's hook
v57 THE TIDE ROLLS: the rhythm section shuffles its sixteenths (swing16 0.65) through the tide, snapping straight at the squeeze
v63 THE SURGE CLIMBS IN FOUR-BAR STEPS: D/C, B-flat/C, D/C, G/Am7 under the low gear, the high gear and the choir; then the tear's D/B-flat
v64 THE LAST OF THE WATER DRAINS: the cross's last four bars lose the band - only the tape choir, contrabass, trombone, sub and dripping off-beat open hats - before the surge lands
v71 THE LINE SPLITS BETWEEN THE TWO SIDES: the second couplet shared - the young near voice sings the near side, the old voice answers the far side, both on 'go' into the crest
v73 AS ONE: the crest's second couplet, where the drums drop out, sung by the young near voice and the old voice together in octaves over the choir
v79 THE FLUTE JOINS THE LAST CHORUS: the shakuhachi doubles the choir's second couplet - E1 itself - two octaves up, the hook on its own instrument one last time
v80 THE LAST EXCHANGE: the young voice sings 'the near side keeps the time' once more from far off, slowed, before the old man's last word
v82 THE SIDES CHANGE PLACES: as the kit arrives the duet returns with its lines swapped - the old voice sings the near side, the young one the far side
v84 THE NAVE FILLS: the pull's last four bars put the tide's chords on the cross's pipe organ, swelling in under 'the tide comes in'
v87 HIGH WATER: under the crest's second couplet the acid line climbs an octave for eight bars, dropping back as the cross ebbs (v86's stop split the song)
v91 THEY TRADE THE TUNE FIRST: the surge's first eight bars hand E1 between the shakuhachi and the far side's trombone and bow, two bars each, before they play as one
v92 THE HYMN: under the cross's organ a soft choir hums the couplet's tune, slowed, in D minor - the congregation in the church by the sea
v93 THE SQUEEZE: the squeeze's first eight bars press the band into one octave - marimba and pans down, root and fretless up - and spring back when the old voice enters
v94 THE TIDE COMES IN BY STAGES: t6's head arrives part by part under t5's tail - pans at bar 3, hats at 5, the old voice at 7, marimba and kora at 9
v95 THEY SING AS ONE AGAIN: after the tear the young voice returns for the last chorus's second couplet, an octave above the old man
v96 AMEN: under the old man's last word the church organ returns and holds a soft B-flat chord for the song's last four bars
v98 THE TUNE TURNS WITH THE TIDE: where the tide's chords turn (bar 41) the shakuhachi plays E1 backwards, twice
v102 THE TIDE PASSES HAND TO HAND: the pull's two 'the tide comes in' become a canon, the near voice and the old man each leading once
v104 EACH TAKES HIS SIDE: one cycle after they sing the crest line together, it comes back split - the young voice the near side, the old man the far side
v105 HE LETS IT GO ON THE TUNE: the old man's 'go' becomes a melisma through E1 itself, D A C G E on one vowel
